title: Time questions review
focus: Ask when and at what time, and answer with everyday time expressions, weekdays and bounded clock times.
targetSkills: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions
Mihin aikaan: answering with clock times

exercises.prompt: Write “When do you eat?” in Finnish. Use sinä (“you”), syöt (“you eat”). Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. Milloin asks when something happens. Put it before the supplied clause: Milloin sinä tulet? (“When are you coming?”). Present-tense Finnish can describe a planned future event when a time word makes the meaning clear. The complete question means “When do you eat”.
requiredSkills: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions
exercises.targetSkill: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking for the time + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)

parts.formation: Milloin asks for the time of an event.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Sinä addresses one person informally.
Syö- + singular second-person -t gives syöt.

optionFeedback.Milloin sinä syöt?: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. Milloin asks when something happens. Put it before the supplied clause: Milloin sinä tulet? optionFeedback.Missä sinä syöt?: This form asks for a different relationship or gives a location instead of the requested source. Match the complete intended meaning.
optionFeedback.Miksi sinä syöt?: Choose the question word for the requested information; keep the complete intended meaning.

exercises.explanation: Answer with a time expression such as tänään (“today”), huomenna (“tomorrow”), nyt (“now”), aamulla (“in the morning”) or illalla (“in the evening”). These taught expressions are learned as complete forms. A full reply includes the appropriate verb; a short time expression also answers milloin. The complete reply means “I eat in the morning”.
requiredSkills: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions
exercises.targetSkill: Milloin: answering with everyday time expressions

parts.formation: Syödä removes -dä and adds -n: syö- + -n gives syön.
Aamu + -lla gives the conventional time expression aamulla.

exercises.prompt: Write “She reads on Wednesday.” in Finnish. Use Hän (“he or she”), lukee (“reads”). Use keskiviikko (“Wednesday”).
exercises.explanation: Hän lukee keskiviikkona. means “She reads on Wednesday.” Koska introduces the reason; the verb agrees with its subject.

parts.formation: Hän refers to one other person without specifying gender.
Use the strong stem luke- and lengthen final e: lukee.
Keskiviikko retains kk before -na: keskiviikkona.

exercises.prompt: Build “I read on Saturday.” in Finnish.
exercises.explanation: A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. A weak stem uses the changed consonants shown in the construction steps; the strong stem keeps the corresponding strong consonants. Use the complete weekday form after the supplied verb: Tulen tiistaina (“I am coming on Tuesday”). A short reply Tiistaina is natural. The ordinary weekday names in this lesson all take -na; do not add an English-style preposition. The complete reply means “I read on Saturday”.

parts.formation: Lukea removes final -a, drops k in the weak stem, and adds -n: lue- + -n gives luen.
Lauantai + -na gives lauantaina.

exercises.prompt: Complete “At what time are you going?”: ____ aikaan sinä menet? Write the full sentence. Use menet (“you go”), sinä (“you”). Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The illative is an into/to form; mihin aikaan uses that form in a time expression. Mihin aikaan asks at what time. Here the phrase asks about time rather than a destination. Use the complete phrase before the supplied clause. Milloin can also request a clock time; mihin aikaan makes that request explicit. The complete question means “At what time are you going”.
requiredSkills: Mihin aikaan: answering with clock times
exercises.targetSkill: Mihin aikaan: answering with clock times

exercises.prompt: Build “I am going at ten o'clock.” in Finnish.
exercises.explanation: For the whole-hour times in this lesson, answer kello + number: kello kaksi (“at two o'clock”). Do not add a separate Finnish word for at. The numbers are supplied; calculating, half-hours and quarter-hours are outside this target. The complete reply means “I am going at ten o'clock”.
